value.Name: Department of Academic Advising
value.Description:
CCP’s Academic Advisors are here to support first time college students and continuing students in good academic standing. Advisors are available on the Main, Northeast Regional, and CAT-C campuses both virtually and in-person.

 

Academic advisors are here to help you ROAR!  

R – Reach your goals 

O – Overcome obstacles 

A – Access Resources 

R – Register for classes 

 

Academic advisors advise students by appointment only based on majors, so that you know the advisor you are speaking with is an expert in your program. This page of our website takes you step-by-step how to find an advisor for your major and schedule an appointment.  

 

Main campus  

Bonnell Building room BG-12 

215-751-8777 

 

We look forward to seeing you soon!

value.Name: Octavius Catto Scholarship
value.Description:
Started in Spring 2021, the Octavius Catto Scholarship is an important anti-poverty initiative designed to put more Philadelphians on the path to success at Community College of Philadelphia.

Combining last-dollar funding with special wrap-around support services, the scholarship will address obstacles like tuition and fees as well as burdens that hit many Philadelphians—especially those living in poverty—particularly hard, including costs associated with food, transportation and books.

Eligible full-time students will receive last-dollar funding, enhanced coaching and advising, and support for food, transportation and books.

The Catto Scholarship is located in the Bonnell Building - B2-33, the main office number is 267-414-2111.
The office is open from 8:30 am - 5:00 pm.

value.Name: Student Veterans of Association
value.Description:
Student Veterans Association (SVA) is committed to enhancing the academic, professional, and personal development of veterans in higher education. Our organization offers a wide range of chapter programs and services designed to foster a supportive community that addresses the unique challenges faced by student veterans. Through these initiatives, we strive to create an environment that not only empowers veterans academically but also equips them with the tools necessary for success beyond the classroom.

In addition to our core mission, SVA is deeply invested in supporting the broader community of student veterans. We recognize that many veterans face challenges related to food security, transportation, and understanding their benefits. To address these issues, we provide resources and assistance aimed at ensuring that every veteran has access to essential support services. By partnering with local organizations and leveraging our network, we aim to alleviate some of the burdens that veterans may encounter, enabling them to focus on their education and personal growth.

Furthermore, SVA is dedicated to empowering veterans to navigate their educational benefits effectively. Our advocacy efforts include workshops and informational sessions that help veterans understand and maximize their entitlements. By fostering a comprehensive understanding of available resources, we aim to remove barriers to education and enhance the overall student experience. Together, we can build a supportive and informed community where every veteran has the opportunity to thrive in their academic and personal pursuits.
value.Summary: Student Veterans Association (SVA) is dedicated to enhancing the academic, professional, and personal growth of veterans in higher education. Through our comprehensive chapter programs, services, and impactful research, we advocate for student veterans.
